title: Comparisons and logic: conditions as testable contracts
goal: Check a range with two conditions and distinguish “and” from “or”.

prerequisites.text: You know comparisons, bool and a range boundary.

sections.title: From the task to an operation
paragraphs: A valid age in 0..120 means age>=0 AND age<=120. && is true only when both parts are true. || is true when at least one part is true. ! reverses truth and falsehood. Comparisons produce bool results.

&& and || evaluate their second part only when needed: a false first part settles && as false; a true first part settles || as true. This short-circuiting can protect division by checking its divisor first. This example only uses safe comparisons.

sections.title: Check a range with two conditions and distinguish “and” from “or”.
trace: Neither bound is violated; bool prints as 1/0.

sections.title: Change one condition and check the prediction
paragraphs: Equality at 120 is valid because of <=.
121 exceeds the upper bound but satisfies the lower one.

sections.title: When the result differs
paragraphs: age>=0 || age<=120 accepts 250 because the first part is true. Range membership needs &&.

sections.title: Now solve your own task
paragraphs: Check score in 0..100; print valid for -1,0,100,101 and explain both bounds.
Practice contains a separate starter. Predict the result before changing your program. Returning to the example does not replace your source.

selfcheck.prompt: What output follows the specified change? Check age=120, then age=121.
selfcheck.feedback: Equality at 120 is valid because of <=. 121 exceeds the upper bound but satisfies the lower one.

selfcheck.prompt: Check score in 0..100; print valid for -1,0,100,101 and explain both bounds.
selfcheck.feedback: Compare the output with the readable reference case below. Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic. For score=-1,0,100,101, valid must be 0,1,1,0. score>=0 || score<=100 incorrectly accepts 101; membership in the range requires &&.

steps.action: Check score in 0..100; print valid for -1,0,100,101 and explain both bounds.
Write your solution in a separate starter; keep your previous work.
Compare actual output with your prediction and explain any difference.

terms.definition: Here, a bool expression describing a property to check.
Built-in && is true when both operands are true; the right operand is skipped when the left is false.
Built-in || is true when at least one operand is true; the right operand is skipped when the left is true.
! reverses true and false after converting the operand to bool.
Skipping the right operand when the left already determines a built-in logical expression’s result.
